en: childlike heart; innocence of a child

examples.en: At an amusement park, I feel like a child again.
A child's drawing is full of a child's innocence.

examples.ko: 어른이 되어도 동심을 잃지 않고 싶어요.
examples.en: Even as an adult, I don't want to lose my childlike heart.
This fairy tale stirs the childlike heart in adults.
When it snowed, my childlike spirit came back.

examples.ko: 동심을 지켜 주고 싶어서 거짓말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to protect the child's innocence, so I couldn't lie.

explain: 어린아이처럼 순수하고 깨끗한 마음이에요. '동심으로 돌아가다', '동심을 잃다', '동심을 지키다'처럼 써요. '천진난만'과 비슷하지만, 그건 아이의 모습 자체에, '동심'은 마음에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: 동심 is the pure, unspoiled heart of a child. It goes with 동심으로 돌아가다, 동심을 잃다 and 동심을 지키다. 천진난만 is similar but describes the child's look and manner, while 동심 focuses on the mind.

en: to be stained with; to be smeared with

examples.en: I touched the wall and paint rubbed off on my hand.

examples.ko: 검은 가방 색이 청바지에 묻어나서 속상해요.
examples.en: I'm upset because the black bag's color rubbed off on my jeans.
Warmth comes through in the way he speaks.
She sang in a voice that carried sadness.

examples.ko: 빨래할 때 색이 묻어나지 않게 따로 빨아요.
examples.en: I wash them separately so the color doesn't run onto others.
It's a painting that shows traces of long effort.

explain: 묻은 것이 다른 곳으로 옮겨질 때도 쓰고, 말투·글·표정에서 마음이나 분위기가 느껴질 때도 써요. 앞의 뜻은 '묻다'(물감이 묻다)와 가깝고, 뒤의 뜻은 '배어나다', '드러나다'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: It is used when something sticky or colored transfers onto another surface, and also when feeling or mood comes through in speech, writing, or expression. The first sense is close to 묻다 as in 물감이 묻다, and the second is similar to 배어나다 and 드러나다.

examples.en: I trembled while watching a scary movie.
I'm so cold my whole body is shaking.
My hands trembled before the presentation.

examples.ko: 아이가 개를 보고 벌벌 떨면서 울었어요.
examples.en: The child saw a dog, shook with fear, and cried.

examples.ko: 선생님 앞에서 벌벌 떨 필요 없어요.
examples.en: There's no need to shake in front of the teacher.

examples.ko: 높은 곳에 올라가니까 다리가 벌벌 떨려요!
examples.en: My legs are shaking since I climbed up somewhere high!

explain: '벌벌'은 무섭거나 추워서 몸이 떠는 모양을 말해요. 늘 '떨다', '떨리다'와 함께 쓰고 '벌벌 떨다'가 하나의 덩어리예요. '덜덜'은 추위나 기계에, '부들부들'은 화나거나 힘줄 때 더 어울려요.
explain_en: 벌벌 shows a body shaking from fear or cold, and it is nearly always used with 떨다 or 떨리다 as 벌벌 떨다. 덜덜 fits cold or machines better, and 부들부들 fits anger or strain.

en: to worry; to bother; to keep someone in suspense

examples.en: I was anxious all day because I didn't hear from them.

examples.ko: 그만 애태우고 결과를 빨리 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Stop keeping me in suspense and tell me the result already.
Don't keep your parents worried for too long.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일부러 답장을 늦게 해서 저를 애태워요.
examples.en: He replies late on purpose to keep me on edge.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리며 애태우던 시간이 길었어요.
examples.en: The time I spent anxiously waiting for my exam results was long.

examples.ko: 합격 발표를 앞두고 애태우는 친구를 위로해 줬어요.
examples.en: I comforted my friend who was fretting before the pass announcement.

explain: '걱정하다'보다 속이 타고 조마조마한 느낌이 훨씬 강해요. 내가 혼자 마음을 졸일 때도 쓰고, 위 예문처럼 남을 애태우게 할 때도 써요. 말할 때는 '애를 태우다'라고 띄어서 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '걱정하다': it carries a feeling of being on pins and needles. You can use it when you fret alone, or, as in the examples, when you make someone else anxious. People also say it as two words, '애를 태우다'.

examples.en: Don't despair just because you failed the exam.
He fell into despair when he heard the news of the accident.
Despairing alone won't solve the problem.

examples.ko: 절망하는 친구에게 따뜻한 말을 해 줬어요.
examples.en: I said kind words to my friend who was in despair.

examples.ko: 모든 걸 잃고 절망한 사람들이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people had lost everything and despaired.
There's no need to despair so early.

explain: 절망하다는 희망이 완전히 없다고 느낄 때 써요. 그냥 '실망하다'는 기대와 달라서 마음이 상하는 정도이고, 절망하다는 훨씬 더 깊고 무거운 말이에요. '절망하지 마세요'처럼 위로할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: 절망하다 is used when you feel there is no hope left at all. '실망하다' is being let down because things didn't match your expectations, while 절망하다 is much deeper and heavier. A common use is comforting someone: '절망하지 마세요'.

examples.ko: 어려운 일을 끝까지 하는 모습이 존경스러워요.
examples.en: The way you see hard things through is admirable.
I met a teacher I admire.
His words and actions were admirable.

examples.ko: 아무도 안 보는데 약속을 지키니까 존경스럽네요.
examples.en: You keep your promise even when no one is watching; that's admirable.
My grandmother's life is so admirable that I bowed my head.

examples.ko: 매일 봉사하는 이웃이 존경스러울 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I find the neighbor who volunteers every day admirable.

explain: '~을 존경하다'는 대상을 '을/를'로 받지만 '~이/가 존경스럽다'는 대상이 '이/가'로 와요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라서 '존경스러워요', '존경스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 그 사람을 보고 저절로 드는 느낌을 말해요.
explain_en: '존경하다' marks its object with '을/를', but with '존경스럽다' the person admired takes '이/가'. It is a 'ㅂ' irregular, so it becomes '존경스러워요' and '존경스러운'. It describes the feeling that arises on seeing that person.

examples.ko: 친구가 칭찬받는 걸 보고 질투심이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I felt jealous when I saw my friend get praised.

examples.ko: 질투심 때문에 그 사람과 말도 하기 싫었어요.
examples.en: Out of jealousy, I didn't even want to talk to that person.

examples.ko: 동생은 질투심이 강해서 장난감을 나눠 쓰지 않아요.
examples.en: My little brother is very jealous, so he won't share his toys.
I laughed on purpose to hide my jealousy.

examples.ko: 그는 질투심에 눈이 멀어 친구를 의심했어요.
examples.en: Blinded by jealousy, he suspected his friend.

examples.ko: 작은 질투심은 사랑하는 사이에서 자주 생겨요.
examples.en: A little jealousy often comes up between people in love.

explain: '질투심이 생기다', '질투심이 강하다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '시기'는 남이 잘되는 걸 싫어하는 마음이고, 질투심은 사랑하는 사람이나 내 것을 빼앗길까 불안한 마음에도 써요. 사람을 말할 때는 '질투가 많다'도 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Common patterns are 질투심이 생기다 and 질투심이 강하다. 시기 is resenting someone else's success, while 질투심 also covers the anxiety of losing someone you love or something you have. For a person, 질투가 많다 is also natural.

en: to remember; to recall; to look back

examples.en: I sometimes think fondly of my school days.
I looked at old photos with my friends and reminisced.
Grandmother smiled as she looked back on her youth.
That song makes me recall last summer.

examples.ko: 우리는 같이 여행한 날을 추억하곤 해요.
examples.en: We often look back on the day we traveled together.
I'm happy because I have a lot to look back on.

explain: '추억하다'는 좋았던 옛날을 따뜻하게 떠올릴 때 써요. 나쁜 기억에는 보통 쓰지 않아요. 일상 대화에서는 '그때가 생각나요', '추억이 있어요'처럼 명사 '추억'을 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 추억하다 is for warmly recalling good times in the past, and is not usually used for bad memories. In daily talk people more often use the noun, as in '추억이 있어요' or '그때가 생각나요'.

dis.h: look back fondly on the past

p.n: 추억하다 means looking back warmly. 기억하다 means plainly remembering.

examples.en: The child broke into a broad smile on getting the present.

examples.ko: 남자는 사진 속에서 청바지를 입고 함박웃음을 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: In the photo, the man is wearing jeans and smiling broadly.
Grandma welcomed me with a big, bright smile.

examples.ko: 합격 소식에 엄마 얼굴에 함박웃음이 가득했어요.
examples.en: Mom's face was full of smiles at the news that I passed.
I saw a photo of my friends smiling broadly.
His big smile put me in a good mood too.

explain: '활짝 웃다'처럼 얼굴 전체로 크게 웃는 모습이 그려져요. '함박웃음을 짓다/웃다/터뜨리다'처럼 써요. 소리 내어 크게 웃는 '폭소'와는 달리 환하게 웃는 모습에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: It paints a picture of a smile that lights up the whole face, like '활짝 웃다'. Use it as '함박웃음을 짓다/웃다/터뜨리다'. Unlike '폭소' (a burst of loud laughter), it is closer to a bright, beaming smile.
